interactions.summary: A student keeps pressing that gluttony has an extra consumptive step beyond taking, while Jiang ends the debate and returns to the logic of rain as punishment.
Students suggest the rain dulls desire or overwhelms the sinner with endless excess, and Jiang keeps asking why that excess is fitting rather than merely unpleasant.

claims.claim: Jiang returns to a simple working definition of gluttony as wanting too much and never stopping that wanting.
A student suggests the punishment works by dulling or numbing desire itself.
claims.temporal_scope: Student interpretation offered during the seminar on 2026-06-21.

claims.claim: Another student argues endless rain mirrors gluttony because it too is a more-and-more excess that never reaches satisfaction.
claims.temporal_scope: Student interpretation offered during the seminar on 2026-06-21.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang resets the whole discussion by reducing gluttony to one relentless structure: too much, with no stopping point.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you want too much and you can never stop from wanting too much
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It keeps later punishment logic tethered to appetite as endless motion rather than to surface symbolism.

chronology_notes.note: This packet shows Jiang using repeated questioning on 2026-06-21 to drive the room from loose analogy toward the structural logic of punishment.
